themes: Manners with the Prophet (peace be upon him)
summary_for_children: Al-Hujurat means The Rooms. It teaches good manners: check news before believing it, make peace between people, don't make fun of others or call them bad names, don't spy or speak badly behind their backs, and know that the best person is the most God-conscious.
environment_concept: A friendly village where each street teaches a manner from the surah: checking news, making peace, no mocking, no nicknames, no spying, no backbiting, and a market square where peoples and tribes meet to know one another.
architecture_and_scenery: Courtyard homes with low walls, a peace bridge between two quarters, a market square with stalls from many lands.

unique_world.visual_theme: A busy village with a well, a bridge over a stream, a bakery and a goat pen around a square with a notice board

primary_mechanic.text: A rumour of four claims is going round. Check each one at its source (well, bridge, oven, pen), then mark each true or not true on the notice board; an unchecked claim cannot be passed on and a wrong mark is refused (49:6). The village is fictional.

unique_world.narrative_structure: The ayah on news, four claims to check, the notice board, then manners and peace
environment_behaviour: a question-mark sign stands at each unchecked source
notes on the board turn green or red as claims are marked
unique_world.learning_objective: Check news before passing it on (49:6), and avoid mocking and suspicion (49:11-12)

story_library.source: Owner's 'Quran Adventure — Children's Story Library' (2026-11-04), first-draft narration for ages about 7-12
story_library.title: The Village of Kind Words
story_library.children_narration: What should we do when someone tells us a rumor? Should we believe it immediately? Surah Al-Hujurat teaches us to check information carefully, avoid mocking others, and respect people from different families and communities. Our differences can help us know one another, not look down on one another.

world_idea.title: The Village of Friendship
world_idea.description: Children investigate a fictional misunderstanding, compare information, and help neighbors resolve it through respectful communication.
